questions.question: India shares longest land border with which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangladesh.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The India-Bangladesh border is the fifth-longest land border in the world and it is approximately 4,096 km long.
 
• The** Radcliffe line (IB)** is the local name for the border between Bangladesh and India.
 
• After India was divided into Pakistan and India, a boundary demarcation line known as The Radcliffe Line was published on **August 17, 1947.**
 
• **Sir Cyril Radcliffe**, the building's architect, inspired its name.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** India-China border** is approximately **3,488 km long.**
 
• The **India-Pakistan **border is approximately **3,323 km long** and it is one of the most heavily **militarized borders **in the world.
 
• India shares its land border with Nepal which is approximately 1,751 km long.
 
• The border between India and Nepal was established by the Treaty of Sugauli in 1816.

questions.question: Pongal is another name for Makar Sankranti, which is celebrated during the same time in various cities of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Tamil Nadu.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pongal is a popular harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu, which falls on the same day as Makar Sankranti.
 
• Makar Sankranti is a Hindu festival that marks the transition of the sun into the zodiac sign of Capricorn (Makara), and is celebrated across India with different names and customs.
 
• Pongal is celebrated for four days, and each day has its own significance - Bhogi, Thai Pongal, Maatu Pongal, and Kaanum Pongal.
 
• The festival is marked by the preparation of traditional dishes like Pongal, sugarcane, and sweetmeats, and the decoration of houses with colourful rangolis and flowers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• While Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, and Kerala also celebrate Makar Sankranti, they have different names for the festival -

 
 
• in Andhra Pradesh it is known as Sankranti,
 
• in Karnataka it is called Suggi, and in
 
• Kerala it is known as Makaravilakku.

questions.question: Which among the following is a cooking procedure in which the sugar in the food gets oxidized, turning into a brown colour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Caramelisation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Caramelisation** is a **cooking procedure** in which the sugar in the food **gets oxidized,** turning into a** brown colour.**
 
• This process involves** heating sugar** to a certain temperature, causing it to break down and form new compounds that give the food a** distinct flavour and colour. **
 
• Caramelisation is commonly used in **cooking and baking** to add flavour and colour to dishes such as** caramel sauce, crundefinedme brundefinedlundefinede, and caramelized onions.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Filtration:** a process of separating solid particles from a liquid by passing it through a** porous material **such as a **filter paper or mesh.**
 
• **Emulsification:** a process of **combining two immiscible liquids** such as oil and water to form a **stable mixture.**
 
• **Bromination:** a chemical reaction that involves the addition of **bromine to a compound,** often used in organic chemistry.

• The major folk dances of **Uttar Pradesh** are** Charkula, ****Raslila****, Kathak, Ramlila, Khyal, Nautanki, Dadra, and Kajri Dance.**

questions.question: Which country is the only country in the world to have both tigers and lions?

__
 
• **India **is the only country in the world to have both **tigers and lions** in the wild.
 
• India is home to the **Bengal tiger**, which is the most common subspecies of tiger found in the country, and the** Asiatic lion**, which is only found in the **Gir Forest National Park **in the state of Gujarat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kenya **is known for its** wildlife, including lions,** but does not have tigers in the wild.
 
• **South Africa** is home to** lions**, but tigers are not native to the country.
 
• **China** is known for its **giant pandas,** but tigers and lions are not native to the country.
 
• It is important to note that while some countries may have tigers and lions in captivity, India is the only country where both species can be found in their **natural habitats.**

questions.question: If we deduct depreciation from GNP the measure of aggregate income that we obtain is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Net National Product.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net National Product (NNP)** is calculated by subtracting **depreciation** from **Gross National Product (GNP)**.
 
• **Depreciation **refers to the** decrease in the value of an asset **over time due to **wear and tear or obsolescence.**
 
• NNP is frequently assessed annually as a way to gauge how well a country is **maintaining minimum production standards**.
 
• Although NNP is frequently used in environmental economics, Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the method that is most frequently used to assess **national income and economic prosperity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP) **is the total value of all **goods and services** produced within a country's borders in a given period, regardless of ownership.
 
• **National Income** is the sum of all incomes earned by **individuals and businesses** within a country's borders in a given period, including wages, profits, and rent.
 
• **Private Income **is the income earned by individuals within a** country's borders **in a given period, including wages, salaries, and dividends.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The scheme has also been criticized for **favoring the ruling party**, as it allows for the sale of **electoral bonds** only through select branches of certain banks, which are believed to be more accessible to the** ruling party's supporters.**

questions.question: Who is the author of the novel, "Oliver Twist"?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Charles Dickens** is the author of the novel **"Oliver Twist".**
 
• The novel was first published as a serial in a magazine called** "Bentley's Miscellany" in 1837-1839.**
 
• The story follows the life of an **orphan boy **named **Oliver Twist **who faces many challenges and hardships in Victorian London.
 
• The novel is known for its vivid portrayal of the social conditions and injustices of the time, particularly in relation to** poverty, crime, and the treatment of children.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

• **Oscar Wilde **was an Irish playwright and author known for his works such as **"The Picture of Dorian Gray" and "The Importance of Being Earnest".**
 
• **Jane Austen** was an English author known for her works such as** "Pride and Prejudice" and "Sense and Sensibility".**

questions.question: Judo has its origin in ancient ______ art of Ju - jitsu.

__
 
• **Judo** is a **Japanese martial art** that originated in the late 19th century.
 
• It was developed by** Jigoro Kano**, who was a practitioner of **Ju-jitsu,** a traditional Japanese martial art.
 
• Ju-jitsu is a **close-combat fighting system** that originated in** feudal Japan **and was used by the samurai.
 
• Judo is based on the principles of Ju-jitsu but emphasizes** throws, pins, and joint locks** rather than strikes and kicks.
 
• Judo became an **Olympic sport in 1964** and is now practiced worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Chinese **martial arts include** Kung Fu,** which is a term that refers to a wide range of styles that emphasize **strikes, kicks, and acrobatic movements.**

questions.question: The slash and burn agriculture is called 'Bewar' or 'Dahiya' in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bewar or Dahiya** is a traditional method of **agriculture** where farmers **cut down and burn a patch of forest** land to create **fertile fields.**
 
• This type of agriculture is practiced in many parts of India, including **Madhya Pradesh**, which is known for its** forests and tribal communities.**
 
• The practice of Bewar or Dahiya is considered** harmful to the environment** as it leads to **deforestation and soil erosion.**
 
• However, it is still widely used by farmers who have** limited access to modern agricultural technologies**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odisha** is also known for its tribal communities who practice** Bewar or Dahiya agriculture.**

 
 
• The state has a rich history of traditional **agriculture practices.**
 
 
 
• **Assam **is known for its** tea plantations and rice cultivation.**
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** is the most populous state in India and is known for its **agriculture and dairy industries. **
 
• **Slash and burn agriculture, **also known as swidden agriculture, is a type of farming that involves **cutting down and burning forests** to create fields for cultivation.
 
 
• This traditional method of farming is practiced in many parts of the world, including the** Amazon rainforest, Southeast Asia, and parts of Africa.**
 
• While it has been practiced for centuries, it is now considered harmful to the environment as it leads to** deforestation and soil erosion.**
 
• Many governments and organizations are working to promote** sustainable agriculture practices** that protect the environment and support local communities.

• **​**He is known for his radical approach to India's independence movement and his** alliance with Nazi Germany and Imperial Japan** during World War II.

questions.question: ______ is the female reproductive part of the flower.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pistil.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** pistil** is the **female reproductive part** of a flower, consisting of three parts: the **stigma, style, and ovary.**
 
• The stigma is the **sticky top of the pistil** that collects** pollen.**
 
• The style is a** tube-like structure **that connects the** stigma to the ovary.**
 
• The ovary contains the** ovules,** which develop into **seeds after fertilization.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **anther and filament **are parts of the** male reproductive system **in flowers, collectively called the **stamen.**
 
• **Filament** is the **slender stalk** that holds the anther in the **flower's male portion.**
 
• The part of the stamen called the** anther** is where** pollen** is made.
 
• The **pollen** is carried to the pistil for** fertilization by insects or wind.**

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution mentions the fundamental duty to safeguard public property and to abjure violence"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 51A(i)**____**.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51A **of the Indian Constitution lays down the **fundamental duties** of every citizen of India. 
 
• **Article 51A (i)** states that it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to** safeguard public property** and to **abjure violence.**
 
• This duty is important to maintain law and order in the country and to ensure that public property is** not damaged or destroyed **by any individual or group.
 
• The duty to** abjure violence** means that citizens should refrain from any kind of violent activities that may harm others or cause **damage to public property.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 51A (g)** mentions the duty of every citizen of India to protect and improve the natural environment including **forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife,** and to have compassion for living creatures.

 
 
• This duty emphasizes the** importance of environmental protection **and **animal welfare.**
 
 
 
• **Article 51A (a) **mentions the duty of every citizen of India to **abide by the Constitution** and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
 
• This duty emphasizes the** importance of patriotism and respect **for national symbols.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A (d)** mentions the duty of every citizen of India to promote** harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood **amongst all the people of India, transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities.
 
 
• This duty emphasizes the importance of **communal harmony and national integration.**

questions.question: Which ruler defeated Humayun in the battle of Chausa and Kannauj?

__
 
• **Battle of Chausa and Kannauj** took place in **1539.**
 
• Sher Shah was a **Pashtun leader **who established the** Sur Empire in North India **after defeating the Mughal Empire.
 
• At the Battle of Chausa on **June 26, 1539,** the army commanded by **Sher Shah Suri defeated** the Mughal forces commanded by Humayun.
 
• Humayun, the Mughal Emperor,** escaped **the situation by jumping into the Ganges, possibly sparing his life. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Islam Shah** was the **successor of Sher Shah **and ruled the Sur Empire after his death.
 
• The** seventh sultan of Bijapur,** **Mohammed Adil Shah, **came to power in **1627.**
 
• He supported the Mughals in their campaigns against the** Ahmednagar Sultanate** during his reign, and in **1636** they and he agreed to a peace treaty.
 
• **Ali Adil Shah II, **a young adult of eighteen, succeeded to the throne of **Bijapur **on the death of Mohammed Adil Shah, Sultan of Bijapur, on **November 4, 1656. **

questions.question: When was the Champaran Agrarian Law passed by the British Government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1918.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Champaran Agrarian Law** was passed by the **British Government **in** 1918.**
 
• This law was enacted to **address the grievances **of the peasants in** Champaran district of Bihar** who were forced to **cultivate indigo **on a portion of their land by the** British planters.**
 
• The law provided for the appointment of a commission to inquire into the** agrarian problems of the district** and to suggest **measures for their redressal.**
 
• The commission was headed by **W.C. Banerjee **and included prominent leaders like** Mahatma Gandhi, Rajendra Prasad and Anugrah Narayan Sinha.**
 
• The recommendations of the commission led to the cancellation of the **oppressive indigo system **and the introduction of** new tenancy laws** that gave more rights to the peasants.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• During British rule in India, the **Tinkathia system** was used to cultivate indigo on** 3/20 of the land.**
 
• **Champaran farmers **were concentrating on growing crops using the Tinkathia system.
 
• Teenkathia translates to three Indigo kathas for** every twenty kathas of land.**
 
• In Bihar, a **Kathaa (Bigha)** is a well-known landholding.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major tribe of South India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dang.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Dang tribe is **not **a major tribe of South India. 
 
• The Dang tribe is actually a tribe from the Dangs district of Gujarat, which is located in western India.
 
• **Toda, Badaga, and Irula** are all major tribes of **South India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Toda tribe and the Badaga tribe are primarily located in the Nilgiri Hills of Tamil Nadu.
 
• The** Toda tribe** is known for their unique language, which is only spoken by **around 2,000 people.**
 
• The** Badaga tribe** has a **matrilineal system of inheritance**, which means that property and titles are passed down through the female line.
 
 
• This tribe is known for their **traditional agriculture practices**.
 
 
 
• The** Irula tribe** is recognized as a **Scheduled Tribe** in India, which means that they are entitled to certain government benefits and protections.
 
 
• The Irula tribe is primarily located in Tamil Nadu and is known for their expertise in snake catching and basket weaving.
